proof_summary: Take \(n=736\). If its least base were greater than 7, every base in a nondecreasing representation by at most four squares would lie between \(8\) and \(\lfloor\sqrt{736}\rfloor=27\); elementary size bounds sharpen these to small finite ranges, and exhaustive checking excludes every one-, two-, three-, and four-square sum, so \(a(736)\le 7\) although \(736>599\).
